column1: # The official suite's optional/format/json-pointer.json carries 34 string
# cases, including RFC 6901 §5's own examples and a thorough set of escape
# rejections. What it leaves open is narrow. The escape-then-literal-digit forms
# "/~01" and "/~00" are absent, so is a bare "//", and so is a percent-encoded
# solidus, which is an ordinary member-name character rather than an escape. The
# remaining rows restate a suite case so this file reads as a whole boundary set
# for the validator's one rule past the leading solidus, that a '~' must be
# Row format: see loadVectorFile in vectors_test.go.

column3: the empty pointer names the whole document
~0 then a literal '1', which spells the member name ~1
%2F is an ordinary member-name character, not an escape
a non-empty pointer must begin with a solidus
an escape does not stand in for the leading solidus
a tilde at the end of a member name escapes nothing
